links.outcome: Generalization of COVID-19 chest X-ray CNN across institutions and X-ray device manufacturers
links.effect: Generalization not observed across devices with different response function types; reduced by 18.9% (p<0.05) for image processing and 9.8% (p<0.05) for inter-institutional differences; adding another manufacturer's images decreased internal performance up to 8%.
links.quote: Nonetheless, generalization was not observed across devices with different types of response function.

links.outcome: Performance drop when applying model to data from different institutions and devices than training data
links.effect: Inter-institutional differences reduced generalization performance by 9.8% (p<0.05); device image-processing reduced it by 18.9% (p<0.05).
links.quote: This factor was the key impediment to achieving broad generalization in our research, followed by the device's image-processing and the inter-institutional differences, which both reduced generalization performance to 18.9% (p < 0.05), and 9.8% (p < 0.05), respectively.

screen.reason: The study empirically assesses the impact of data heterogeneity across different institutions and X-ray device manufacturers/response functions on algorithm generalization, providing evidence on local validation and domain shift considerations prior to deployment.
